chapterNote: The Great Hallel — sung at Passover after the Egyptian Hallel; its refrain was already on the lips of Solomon's choirs when the glory filled the temple (2 Chronicles 5:13; 7:3) and of the singers Jehoshaphat sent out ahead of his army (2 Chronicles 20:21). It is Israel's most antiphonal psalm: twenty-six lines from the leader, and after every one the same answer from the whole people — for His covenant love holds firm forever. The lines march through everything: the God above gods and Lord above lords; creation, from the heavens framed by understanding to the sun and moon on their shifts; the exodus, from the tenth plague through the sea cut in pieces and Pharaoh shaken off into it; the wilderness, the Transjordan kings Sihon and Og, the land handed over as an inheritance; and then the tense changes and the singers put themselves in — who remembered us when we were low, who tore us free, who feeds every living creature. The refrain is the theology: sung over a slain firstborn and a drowned army as readily as over the stars and the bread, because in Israel's confession God's judgments on the oppressor and His kindness to the oppressed are one and the same chesed. Twenty-six times, so that no one could leave without knowing the one thing.

1.text: Give thanks to the LORD — how good He is! — for His covenant love holds firm forever.
1.amp: O give thanks [yadah] unto the LORD [YHWH]; for He is good [tov]: for His mercy [chesed — covenant love] endures for ever [olam].
1.notes: The Great Hallel, sung after the Egyptian Hallel at Passover: twenty-six calls and twenty-six answers, ki le-olam chasdo (H5769, H2617) — 'for to eternity is His covenant love' — the congregation's response to every line. hodu (H3034) opens it: thanksgiving as the only fitting reply to goodness (tov, H2896).

2.text: Thank the God who stands above all gods — for His covenant love holds firm forever.
2.amp: O give thanks [yadah] unto the God [Elohim] of gods [elohim]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
2.notes: Elohe ha-elohim (H430): the God of the gods — not a concession that they exist as rivals but a ranking that leaves them nothing. The refrain answers even this: His supremacy is exercised as chesed.

3.text: Thank the Lord who rules above all lords — for His covenant love holds firm forever.
3.amp: O give thanks [yadah] to the Lord [Adon] of lords [adonim]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
3.notes: Adone ha-adonim (H113): Lord of lords, the title Revelation 19:16 hangs on the returning Christ. Three summonses to thank (vv. 1-3), each aimed higher; then the reasons begin.

4.text: To the One who alone performs great wonders — for His covenant love holds firm forever;
4.amp: To Him who alone does [asah] great [gadol] wonders [pala]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
4.notes: le-oseh niphlaot gedolot levaddo (H6213, H6381, H1419): He alone works the great wonders — levaddo, by Himself, with no assistant. The creation and exodus catalogues that follow are the itemized list of those wonders.

5.text: who framed the heavens by His understanding — for His covenant love holds firm forever;
5.amp: To Him that by wisdom [tebunah — understanding, discernment] made [asah] the heavens [shamayim]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
5.notes: bi-tebunah (H8394): the shamayim (H8064) built by discernment — the same wisdom Proverbs 3:19 credits; creation was thought before it was made (asah, H6213). And the refrain insists: intelligence that vast is loyal love in action.

6.text: who stretched the dry land out over the waters — for His covenant love holds firm forever;
6.amp: To Him that stretched out [raqa — beat out, spread flat] the earth [eretz] above the waters [mayim]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
6.notes: roqa ha-aretz al ha-mayim (H7554, H776, H4325): the earth beaten out flat — the metalworker's hammering-verb — above the waters, the ancient picture of dry land held up over the deep. Chesed as engineering.

7.text: who crafted the great lights — for His covenant love holds firm forever:
7.amp: To Him that made [asah] great [gadol] lights [or]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam]:
7.notes: orim gedolim (H216, H1419), the great lights of Genesis 1:16 — made, asah (H6213), not divine. The refrain follows the sun and moon around: the pagan gods are reduced to evidence of the true God's kindness.

8.text: the sun to hold its daily dominion — for His covenant love holds firm forever;
8.amp: The sun [shemesh] to rule ['for the rulings by day', memshalah, the KJV margin] by day [yom]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam]:
8.notes: The shemesh le-memshelet ba-yom (H8121, H4475, H3117) — delegated dominion, Genesis 1's 'to rule'. Even the sun is an appointee; every sunrise is a chesed arriving on schedule.

9.text: the moon with the stars to hold their nightly dominion — for His covenant love holds firm forever.
9.amp: The moon [yareach] and stars [kokab] to rule [memshalah] by night [layil]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
9.notes: yareach ve-kokabim le-memshelot ba-lailah (H3394, H3556, H4475, H3915): the moon and stars share the night shift. The refrain has now been sung over the whole cosmos; the next line drops into history.

10.text: To the One who struck Egypt down through its firstborn — for His covenant love holds firm forever;
10.amp: To Him that smote [nakah] Egypt [Mitsrayim] in their firstborn [bekor]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam]:
10.notes: le-makkeh Mitsrayim bi-bekhorehem (H5221, H4714, H1060): the tenth plague — and the congregation answers 'for His covenant love holds firm forever' to a line about dead firstborn. Judgment on the oppressor IS chesed to the oppressed; the psalm refuses to separate them.

11.text: and brought Israel out from their midst — for His covenant love holds firm forever,
11.amp: And brought out [yatsa] Israel [Yisrael] from among [tavek] them: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam]:
11.notes: va-yotse Yisrael mi-tokham (H3318, H3478, H8432): the exodus-verb, brought out from their midst. Every Passover table that sang this line was a family still standing in the doorway of that night.

12.text: with a mighty hand and an arm reached out at full length — for His covenant love holds firm forever.
12.amp: With a strong [chazaq] hand [yad], and with a stretched out [natah] arm [zeroa]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
12.notes: be-yad chazaqah u-bi-zeroa netuyah (H3027, H2389, H2220, H5186): Deuteronomy's fixed formula for the exodus (cf. Deuteronomy 4:34; 5:15) — the strong hand and the arm extended to its full reach. Chesed has muscles.

13.text: To the One who cut the Red Sea apart into pieces — for His covenant love holds firm forever;
13.amp: To Him which divided [gazar — cut] the Red [suph — reed] sea [yam] into parts [gezer — cut-pieces]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam]:
13.notes: le-gozer yam suph li-gezarim (H1504, H3220, H5488, H1506): He CUT the yam suph, the Sea of Reeds, into gezarim, cut-pieces — the sea sliced through like a thing to be walked between. Not parted gently; severed.

14.text: and walked Israel straight through its midst — for His covenant love holds firm forever;
14.amp: And made Israel [Yisrael] to pass through [abar] the midst [tavek] of it: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam]:
14.notes: ve-heebir Yisrael be-tokho (H5674, H3478, H8432): the passing-through verb — abar, which by the old etymology stands behind 'Hebrew' (ivri, 'one from across'; Scripture ties the name to the ancestor Eber, Genesis 10:21) — through the middle of the cut sea. The people whose very name was heard as 'crossers' made their defining crossing here.

15.text: but shook Pharaoh and his army loose into that same Red Sea — for His covenant love holds firm forever.
15.amp: But overthrew ['shaked off', naar, the KJV margin] Pharaoh [Paroh] and his host [chayil — army] in the Red [suph] sea [yam]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
15.notes: ve-nier Paroh ve-chelo be-yam suph (H5287, H6547, H2428, H3220): nier, 'shook off' — the KJV margin's word — as a man shakes crumbs from a cloth; Pharaoh and his chayil, his military might, flicked into the sea. The refrain is sung over drowned chariots: mercy to Israel and judgment on Egypt were one act.

16.text: To the One who guided His people across the wilderness — for His covenant love holds firm forever.
16.amp: To Him which led [yalak] His people [am] through the wilderness [midbar]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
16.notes: le-molikh ammo ba-midbar (H3212, H5971, H4057): forty years of guidance in the midbar compressed to one line — the manna, the water, the pillar, all under one refrain.

17.text: To the One who struck mighty kings down — for His covenant love holds firm forever;
17.amp: To Him which smote [nakah] great [gadol] kings [melek]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam]:
17.notes: le-makkeh melakhim gedolim (H5221, H4428, H1419): the same makkeh-verb as Egypt's firstborn (v. 10), now for the Transjordan campaign of Numbers 21. Chesed includes clearing the road.

18.text: and slew majestic kings — for His covenant love holds firm forever:
18.amp: And slew [harag] famous [addir — majestic, mighty] kings [melek]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam]:
18.notes: va-yaharog melakhim addirim (H2026, H4428, H117): slain majestic kings — addirim, the 'mighty ones', a word used elsewhere of God Himself. Their majesty did not survive contact with His.

19.text: Sihon, the Amorites' king — for His covenant love holds firm forever;
19.amp: Sihon [Sichon] king [melek] of the Amorites [Emori]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam]:
19.notes: Sichon melekh ha-Emori (H5511, H4428, H567): the first named king, who refused Israel passage and lost his kingdom for it (cf. Numbers 21:21-26). The congregation answered his name with the refrain: a defeated enemy as an item of thanksgiving.

20.text: and Og, Bashan's king — for His covenant love holds firm forever;
20.amp: And Og [Og] the king [melek] of Bashan [Bashan]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam]:
20.notes: Og melekh ha-Bashan (H5747, H4428, H1316): the giant of the iron bed (cf. Deuteronomy 3:11), the last of the Rephaim. His fall was sung for a thousand years by the descendants of the people he meant to crush.

21.text: and handed their land over as an inheritance — for His covenant love holds firm forever,
21.amp: And gave [natan] their land [eretz] for an heritage [nachalah — inheritance]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam]:
21.notes: ve-natan artsam le-nachalah (H5414, H776, H5159): their land given as nachalah, the inheritance-word — conquest reframed as bequest. Israel did not seize; it inherited what God had handed over.

22.text: an inheritance for Israel His servant — for His covenant love holds firm forever.
22.amp: Even an heritage [nachalah] unto Israel [Yisrael] His servant [ebed]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
22.notes: nachalah le-Yisrael abdo (H5159, H3478, H5650): inheritance for Israel HIS SERVANT — the land came with a job. Servants who forgot the Master would later lose the estate, which is exactly where verse 23 begins.

23.text: Who remembered us when we were brought low — for His covenant love holds firm forever;
23.amp: Who remembered [zakar] us in our low estate [shephel — our lowness]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam]:
23.notes: she-be-shiphlenu zakhar lanu (H8216, H2142): in our lowness He remembered us — most naturally the exile's verse, the low estate after the estate was lost. The psalm's tense shifts from 'them' to 'us': the singers put themselves in the story.

24.text: and wrenched us loose from those who pressed us hard — for His covenant love holds firm forever;
24.amp: And has redeemed [paraq — torn away, wrenched free] us from our enemies [tsar — adversaries, the ones who press]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
24.notes: va-yiphreqenu mi-tsarenu (H6561, H6862): paraq, to tear away, wrench loose — from tsarim, adversaries, a word whose consonants in Hebrew also spell 'narrow' and 'distress', so that the enemy and the tight place sound alike. Rescue as a violent extraction from a tight place.

25.text: who provides bread for every living creature — for His covenant love holds firm forever.
25.amp: Who gives [natan] food [lechem — bread] to all flesh [basar]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
25.notes: noten lechem le-khol basar (H5414, H3899, H1320): bread for ALL flesh — not Israel only but every creature that eats. After redemption's particular history, providence's universal table (cf. Psalm 145:15-16; Matthew 6:26).

26.text: Lift up thanks to the God of the heavens — for His covenant love holds firm forever.
26.amp: O give thanks [yadah] unto the God [El] of heaven [shamayim]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
26.notes: hodu le-El ha-shamayim (H3034, H410, H8064): the closing hodu, now to the God of the heavens — a title Abraham already knew (Genesis 24:7) but that became the exiles' characteristic name for Him in Ezra and Nehemiah's day (Ezra 1:2; Nehemiah 1:4). Twenty-six refrains, one conclusion: His covenant love holds firm forever.
